{
  "findings": [

      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",

      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Minimum token schema does not allow arbitrary token fields",
      "body": "The computed keys in minimumTokenResponseSchema (e.g. [z.string().toString()]) do not create a catch-all/index signature in Zod; they only add fixed, unintended properties. As a result, when app credential sharing is enabled, normal OAuth fields such as refresh_token, expires_in, expiry_date, and provider-specific fields are stripped from the parsed token. This causes loss of token data and broken refresh flows. Use z.record/catchall or an explicit schema."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 26,
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Placeholder refresh_token is written into credentials",
      "body": "If the parsed token lacks refresh_token, the helper assigns the literal string 'refresh_token' as the refresh token. Because the minimum schema strips refresh_token from real responses, this placeholder can be persisted over a real refresh token or stored when none was returned, making future OAuth refreshes impossible. It should preserve the previous refresh token or fail when a required refresh token is missing."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 97,
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Google credential update stores SafeParse result instead of token data",
      "body": "parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod SafeParse result, but this code stores that entire result as the credential key. The saved key becomes { success: true, data: ... } rather than the credential object. Subsequent parsing of credential.key with googleCredentialSchema will fail, breaking Google Calendar token refresh for all modes. The code should store parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data or change the helper to return data."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 8,
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Sync path returns a fetch Response while callers expect provider-specific response objects",
      "body": "When sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT; otherwise it returns the provider refresh function's result. Callers are written for the provider result: Google expects res.data, HubSpot expects a token object with accessToken/expiresIn, and Zoho Bigin/CRM expect Axios responses with .data. With sync enabled these callers read undefined properties, throw, or save invalid credentials. The sync response must be normalized to the shape expected by each app."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 96,
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "prisma is used but not imported",
      "body": "The added credential update calls prisma.credential.update, but the file does not import prisma from @calcom/prisma. This will fail type checking or throw a ReferenceError at runtime when the Salesforce calendar service attempts to refresh credentials."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 106,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Salesforce client is created with stale access token after refresh",
      "body": "After fetching a new Salesforce access token, the code persists it but then constructs jsforce.Connection using credentialKey.access_token, which is the old token read before the refresh. If the old token is expired or rotated, the connection will not be authorized. Use the newly parsed access token when creating the connection."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 93,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Zoho Bigin sends credential ID as calcomUserId",
      "body": "refreshOAuthTokens's third parameter is used as the Cal.com user ID sent to the external sync endpoint. Bigin passes credentialId here, so the sync payload contains the credential row ID instead of the user ID. The external token provider will not be able to identify the correct user. Pass credential.userId (or store it in the service) instead."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts",
      "line": 92,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Zoom refresh uses wrong app slug",
      "body": "The sync helper is called with appSlug 'zoomvideo', but the Zoom app credential is stored/identified by the slug 'zoom' (for example, the OAuth callback creates appId 'zoom'). The external sync endpoint will receive an unrecognized app slug and may return the wrong token or fail. Use 'zoom'."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 73,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Updating synced credential does not clear invalid flag",
      "body": "The webhook update path only updates key. If the existing credential has invalid: true from a previous failed refresh, the newly synced valid key remains marked invalid and may be skipped by adapters. The update should also set invalid: false when accepting new synced credentials."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 62,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Find-then-create/update credential is not atomic",
      "body": "The endpoint performs findFirst followed by create/update without a transaction or unique-constraint upsert. Concurrent webhook calls for the same user/app can both miss an existing credential and create duplicate credentials, or overwrite each other in an undefined order. This can cause stale or ambiguous OAuth credentials. Use atomic updateMany/create or a transaction with proper uniqueness."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 8,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Outbound credential sync request has no authentication or HTTPS enforcement",
      "body": "The outbound request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug and does not include a shared secret, signature, or client authentication. It also does not require HTTPS. If the endpoint is reachable outside a trusted internal network, it can be abused to obtain user tokens, and token responses may be exposed in transit. Add authentication/signing and enforce HTTPS."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 17,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Webhook handler accepts all HTTP methods",
      "body": "The handler does not check req.method. A GET or other non-POST request will still execute the webhook logic and likely throw during body parsing, returning a 500 instead of a 405. Restrict the route to POST."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 75,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "perf",
      "title": "Salesforce client refreshes token unconditionally",
      "body": "getClient always calls the Salesforce OAuth token endpoint before creating a connection, even if the stored access token has not expired. This creates unnecessary refresh requests and can cause rate limiting or latency. Check the token expiry and refresh only when needed."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 17,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "No automated tests for credential sync webhook",
      "body": "This adds a security-sensitive webhook that can create/replace OAuth credentials and changes token refresh flows across many apps, but no automated tests are included for authentication, encryption/decryption, invalid payloads, duplicate handling, or sync-enabled refresh behavior. Without tests these regressions are easy to reintroduce."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Minimum token schema does not allow arbitrary token fields
findings.body: The computed keys in minimumTokenResponseSchema (e.g. [z.string().toString()]) do not create a catch-all/index signature in Zod; they only add fixed, unintended properties. As a result, when app credential sharing is enabled, normal OAuth fields such as refresh_token, expires_in, expiry_date, and provider-specific fields are stripped from the parsed token. This causes loss of token data and broken refresh flows. Use z.record/catchall or an explicit schema.

findings.title: Placeholder refresh_token is written into credentials
findings.body: If the parsed token lacks refresh_token, the helper assigns the literal string 'refresh_token' as the refresh token. Because the minimum schema strips refresh_token from real responses, this placeholder can be persisted over a real refresh token or stored when none was returned, making future OAuth refreshes impossible. It should preserve the previous refresh token or fail when a required refresh token is missing.

findings.title: Google credential update stores SafeParse result instead of token data
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod SafeParse result, but this code stores that entire result as the credential key. The saved key becomes { success: true, data: ... } rather than the credential object. Subsequent parsing of credential.key with googleCredentialSchema will fail, breaking Google Calendar token refresh for all modes. The code should store parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data or change the helper to return data.

findings.title: Sync path returns a fetch Response while callers expect provider-specific response objects
findings.body: When sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT; otherwise it returns the provider refresh function's result. Callers are written for the provider result: Google expects res.data, HubSpot expects a token object with accessToken/expiresIn, and Zoho Bigin/CRM expect Axios responses with .data. With sync enabled these callers read undefined properties, throw, or save invalid credentials. The sync response must be normalized to the shape expected by each app.

findings.title: prisma is used but not imported
findings.body: The added credential update calls prisma.credential.update, but the file does not import prisma from @calcom/prisma. This will fail type checking or throw a ReferenceError at runtime when the Salesforce calendar service attempts to refresh credentials.

findings.title: Salesforce client is created with stale access token after refresh
findings.body: After fetching a new Salesforce access token, the code persists it but then constructs jsforce.Connection using credentialKey.access_token, which is the old token read before the refresh. If the old token is expired or rotated, the connection will not be authorized. Use the newly parsed access token when creating the connection.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sends credential ID as calcomUserId
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens's third parameter is used as the Cal.com user ID sent to the external sync endpoint. Bigin passes credentialId here, so the sync payload contains the credential row ID instead of the user ID. The external token provider will not be able to identify the correct user. Pass credential.userId (or store it in the service) instead.

findings.title: Zoom refresh uses wrong app slug
findings.body: The sync helper is called with appSlug 'zoomvideo', but the Zoom app credential is stored/identified by the slug 'zoom' (for example, the OAuth callback creates appId 'zoom'). The external sync endpoint will receive an unrecognized app slug and may return the wrong token or fail. Use 'zoom'.

findings.title: Updating synced credential does not clear invalid flag
findings.body: The webhook update path only updates key. If the existing credential has invalid: true from a previous failed refresh, the newly synced valid key remains marked invalid and may be skipped by adapters. The update should also set invalid: false when accepting new synced credentials.

findings.title: Find-then-create/update credential is not atomic
findings.body: The endpoint performs findFirst followed by create/update without a transaction or unique-constraint upsert. Concurrent webhook calls for the same user/app can both miss an existing credential and create duplicate credentials, or overwrite each other in an undefined order. This can cause stale or ambiguous OAuth credentials. Use atomic updateMany/create or a transaction with proper uniqueness.

findings.title: Outbound credential sync request has no authentication or HTTPS enforcement
findings.body: The outbound request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug and does not include a shared secret, signature, or client authentication. It also does not require HTTPS. If the endpoint is reachable outside a trusted internal network, it can be abused to obtain user tokens, and token responses may be exposed in transit. Add authentication/signing and enforce HTTPS.

findings.title: Webhook handler accepts all HTTP methods
findings.body: The handler does not check req.method. A GET or other non-POST request will still execute the webhook logic and likely throw during body parsing, returning a 500 instead of a 405. Restrict the route to POST.

findings.title: Salesforce client refreshes token unconditionally
findings.body: getClient always calls the Salesforce OAuth token endpoint before creating a connection, even if the stored access token has not expired. This creates unnecessary refresh requests and can cause rate limiting or latency. Check the token expiry and refresh only when needed.

findings.title: No automated tests for credential sync webhook
findings.body: This adds a security-sensitive webhook that can create/replace OAuth credentials and changes token refresh flows across many apps, but no automated tests are included for authentication, encryption/decryption, invalid payloads, duplicate handling, or sync-enabled refresh behavior. Without tests these regressions are easy to reintroduce.
